topic: the Thyiades -- real Delphi women who performed Dionysian rituals on Mount Parnassus, once stranded by a blizzard
title: Real Women Once Got Stranded Performing a 'Mythical' Greek Ritual
description: AI-narrated commentary on the Thyiades -- real women in ancient Delphi who performed the same ecstatic Dionysian rituals as Greek mythology's maenads, as an official biennial civic rite on Mount Parnassus, and the time a snowstorm nearly trapped them there.

hook_candidates.text: Real women once got stranded on a mountain in a blizzard — the exact ritual you thought only existed in Greek myth.
The maenads from Greek myth weren't fiction — Delphi ran the same ritual as an actual government-sanctioned event, snowstorms included.
Why would an ancient Greek city send women up a freezing mountain, in the dark, on purpose, every other year?
Every other winter for centuries, a select group of Delphi women climbed a mountain at night to dance for Dionysus — until one year, a blizzard nearly stranded them there for good.

payoff_mechanism: Cities folded this ecstatic Dionysian ritual into their official religious calendar every other year specifically so the god's mythic wildness had a structured, government-approved outlet instead of spreading uncontrolled through the population, which is exactly why real magistrates organized a rescue party when a Delphi procession actually got trapped by a snowstorm on Mount Parnassus.
share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who insists all Greek myths are pure fiction, because they want to prove real women actually performed the maenads' ritual.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume the maenads from Greek myth are purely fictional stories, but real women actually got stranded on a mountain performing that same ritual.

sources.note: Academic study (McInerney) on the historical Thyiades of Delphi, women who made biennial ritual ascents of Mount Parnassus for Dionysus.
Confirms the Pausanias-sourced tradition of the Thyiades performing ecstatic Dionysian rites on Mount Parnassus.
Describes the biennial Dionysian rites at Delphi and Plutarch's account of a Thyiades procession rescued from a Parnassus snowstorm.

beats.text: Real women once got **stranded** on a mountain in a blizzard — the exact ritual you thought only existed in Greek myth.
They were the **Thyiades** — real Delphi women who climbed Parnassus every other winter, part of the city's **official** religious calendar.
**Plutarch** recorded one procession trapped by snow so bad, magistrates had to send a real rescue party up the mountain.
So the maenads weren't fiction — real women braved that **snowstorm** on purpose. Follow if myths like this are more real than you'd think.
